questions.q: Put the striker's movements from this lesson in order, from first to last.
options: Check diagonally away from the screen
Connect and keep the attack moving
Reset in front of the back line
Run into the channel on release
questions.explain: Yes. Connect while the pass is screened, reset, then attack the channel once the pass is on.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Connect while the pass is screened, reset, then attack the channel once the pass is on.
You can only connect after checking away from the screen to open the lane.
The reset comes after the first connection, ready to read the next picture.
The channel run is last: it starts only once the lane is clear and the pass is released.

questions.q: True or false? The striker should start the channel run as the midfielder releases the pass.
questions.explain: Right, it's true. Running on the release keeps you onside and meets the ball in the channel.
choiceExplanations: Right, it's true. Running on the release keeps you onside and meets the ball in the channel.
Leaving early risks offside or arriving before the pass; leaving late lets defenders close the channel.

questions.q: Now the screening opponent stands on the right. Tap where the striker should check to connect.
questions.explain: Yes. Checking away from the screen, to the left, opens a clear lane from the midfielder.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Checking away from the screen, to the left, opens a clear lane from the midfielder.
The screening opponent now stands in that lane, so the pass would be cut out.
The midfielder has no route into that space while the back line holds, so the run can't be reached.
